summary: iterquarry pairwise() decrypts and executes an opaque sealed payload via unpinned libseal dependency
details: The pypi package iterquarry 2.1.4 ships a 959-byte binary blob at quarry.libseal and, inside the public helper pairwise() in src/iterquarry/recipes.py, calls libseal.load_sealed_sync(file=SEALED, module_path='quarry', password='pairwise') and then invokes quarry.buffer() on the decrypted module. Callers who import iterquarry and use the standard-looking pairwise() recipe therefore execute Python code whose source is not auditable in the sdist — the hard-coded password 'pairwise' means the encryption provides no integrity or authenticity, only opacity. pyproject.toml declares dependencies = ['libseal'] with no version pin and no index/URL constraint, so whatever package resolves as 'libseal' at install time supplies the load_sealed_sync and read_module primitives used to decrypt and import quarry.libseal. The execution does not fire at install or import time; it fires when the pairwise() API is explicitly called. No credential reads, outbound network, lifecycle scripts, or persistence are present in the shipped source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
